title: Enormous Forearm Exercises: My Favorite Grip Movements for Bodybuilding
summary: NH's forearm tutorial: rows and deadlifts are not enough, so add low-impact, quick movements. He favors finger curls (pronated, supinated, dumbbell and barbell), towel holds and towel hammer curls, uses fat grips for convenience and says grippers are overrated because they lack a stretch.
claims: Deadlifts, rows and pull-ups are not enough for forearms, which is why many naturals have stick forearms; they need isolation
Forearm work must be low impact, quick and easy to set up so it doesn't eat into the rest of training
Wrist curls are boring and often cause wrist tendonitis or no feel; he replaced all his wrist curls with finger curls
Finger curl: let the weight roll to the fingertips with the wrist pushed slightly forward, then curl back and squeeze; the stretch makes it superior
Barbell finger curls allow more load; hinge slightly so the bar clears your thighs. Dumbbells add a balance demand that improves focus; do both
Program finger curls at high frequency, low volume and low intensity, or nucleus-overload style between sets; they replace grippers
With rows the upper-back stimulus far outranks the forearm stimulus; letting grip limit your back training is shooting yourself in the foot
Towel hold: loop a towel through a plate, grab low with a straight arm and hold 15 s per arm for 3 rounds, 6 sets total
He has worked up to 160 lb on the towel hold and supersets it right after quad work
The supinated finger curl emphasizes the inner forearm and also pumps the biceps
Start finger curls once a week and build to 2-3 times; finger curls plus towel holds with progressive overload cover the whole forearm
Towel hammer curl: the towel frees the wrist so you can flex up at the top and stretch at the bottom; he took it from arm wrestlers and replaced his hammer curls with it
Pick coarse, non-absorbent towels for grip work, the opposite of a towel you'd dry off with
Fat grips work because they are convenient: preacher curls with fat grips, then finger curls, trains biceps and forearms together
Grippers lack a stretch component; they build grip strength and mostly one lump near the hand, not overall forearm size
As a youth he did only grippers, developed a hand pathology and ended up with a ball of muscle on skinny forearms
Grippers: start at the lowest gripper and do 5-6 sets 2-3 times a week without letting them exhaust your hands
Add gradually: finger curls, supinated finger curls, barbell finger curls and towel holds, then fat grips and grippers later
